gen-fs-nippo-gf-liter: Technical to the core, Nippo has small letters nearly capital-tall and wire-cut. Liter below keeps no stroke contrast and gives wide mouths to its round forms, so it can take a modest size.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-mada: Nippo draws neon-tube letters, glowing at a single line thickness. Mada, with its towering midzone and curves that refuse to close, is what makes the pair stand out.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-martel-sans: Sharp as cut wire: Nippo leaves the single-width trail of a rolling-ball pen across every heading. But Martel Sans keeps generous openings in every curve and a high mean line across each word.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-miriam-libre: Nippo sets small letters nearly as tall as capitals. Miriam Libre follows with the weight of drawn wire and a lowercase of cast-iron stature, so the two stand tall together.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Mochiy Pop One hangs its very large lowercase like clothespins on a long line. But Nippo is best at wire-cut, capital-tall display lettering, while Mochiy Pop One is best at a steady single stroke width.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-montserrat-underline: Nippo keeps its small letters almost capital-sized, with strokes that look cut from wire. And Montserrat Underline lets its counters breathe, with lowercase oversized beside its own capitals.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Noto Kufi Arabic feels modern and clean, with a welcoming gap in its c. But Nippo is at its best as a rope-thin outline, while Noto Kufi Arabic does best with capitals barely above lowercase.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Nippo holds the steady line of a technical drafting pen, with small letters nearly capital-tall. And it earns its keep big and short, with Noto Sans Adlam keeping its curve endings well apart beneath.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-adlam-unjoined: Nippo holds its line thickness firm, with small letters standing almost capital-sized. And Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined gives curve ends generous room from the stem, with little height difference between cases.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hier: Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs reads modern, its terminal tips pointing outward and x-height rising near cap height. Yet Nippo, with stylus-steady stroke weight and wire-cut letters, is what sharpens the whole pairing.
